claude.label: Claude
claude.description: Base seat. Same delegation law as the role seats: Paseo seats are the only delegation surface, no in-session subagents.

supervisor.label: Supervisor-of-record
supervisor.description: Governance front door, process memory, Paseo lifecycle

lead.label: Lead-of-record
lead.description: Router and binding arbiter — planning, coordination, acceptance

peer.label: Peer
peer.description: Independent engineering peer; disposition (Engineer/Architect/Reviewer/Scout) set per task brief. Owner directive 2026-09-12: fast mode stays OFF on this seat too. Here it means the Claude toggle - a different feature from the Codex one on codex-peer, same id, and it was already off on every peer seat. Paseo exposes no provider key that hides it: the Claude provider surfaces it for any model whose manifest carries supportsFastMode, which is every Opus entry below. Dropping the Opus models is the only way to make the toggle disappear and the owner declined that, so the peer keeps Opus and this line is the record.

codex-peer.label: Codex Peer
codex-peer.description: Bounded engineering collaborator on CLIProxy-routed DeepSeek; no Paseo tools. duckling-oci runs CLIProxyAPI with OpenCodeGo/deepseek-v4.1-flash only, so this is the one model. codex-room reads CLIPROXY_API_KEY from the daemon environment (systemd EnvironmentFile ~/.config/cliproxy.env). deepseek-v4.1-flash is the declared default in BOTH this table and ~/.codex/peer.config.toml; keep those two in step. Fast mode stays off: do not pass featureValues.fast_mode to create_agent here.

gemini-peer.label: Gemini Peer
gemini-peer.description: duckling-oci: agy 1.2.14 linux_arm64 from the official installer at ~/.local/bin/agy; agy-acp built on the host from ~/.local/src/agy-acp (the locally patched tree, see its LOCAL-PATCHES.md); Google sign-in copied from the Mac token file. PATH carries ~/.npm-global/bin for the paseo CLI. Otherwise identical to the Mac entry: Bounded engineering/scout collaborator on Gemini via the agy-acp ACP bridge. Mirrors codex-peer's shape: no Paseo tools. Enforced by params.supportsMcpServers=false, which is the ONLY lever that works here - `disallowedTools:['mcp__paseo']`, the mechanism used on peer and codex-peer, does not reach an ACP client. MCP is therefore all-or-nothing on this seat, and it is off. Built on Paseo's generic ACP branch (extends:'acp' -> GenericACPAgentClient). THREE PROPERTIES OF THAT BRANCH ARE LOAD-BEARING AND WERE VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED SOURCE, not assumed: (1) the acp branch builds its client from {logger,command,env,providerId,label,providerParams} only, so `disallowedTools` on this entry would be silently DROPPED - it is deliberately absent here rather than present and inert; (2) the derived definition carries modes:[] and defaultModeId:null, so this seat has NO permission modes - plan-mode pinning is unavailable and the ACP agent's own prompt flow is the only gate; (3) neither acp-agent.js nor generic-acp-agent.js reads systemPrompt or appendSystemPrompt, so ~/.paseo/orchestration/roles/*.md CANNOT be injected into this seat by any Paseo mechanism. A seat here therefore carries no role law, no role-gate.sh (a Claude Code PreToolUse hook), and no ~/.claude/skills surface. PREREQUISITE, MET 2026-09-13: agy (antigravity) 1.2.2 mac_arm64 is installed at ~/.local/bin/antigravity with an `agy` symlink; agy-acp is built from ~/.local/src/agy-acp and installed at ~/.local/bin/agy-acp. Verified end to end on that date: ACP initialize, session/new, and a full session/prompt turn that streamed an agent_message_chunk and closed with stopReason=end_turn. `env.PATH` above is load-bearing - agy-acp spawns the CLI as a bare Command::new("agy") (adapter.rs:57,634) resolved from PATH, and the daemon's own PATH does not carry ~/.local/bin. The earlier concern that this machine's conversation store was the wrong format is RESOLVED and was a false alarm: ~/.gemini/antigravity/ is the Antigravity IDE (protobuf), a different product; the CLI created ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/ (SQLite) on first run, which is exactly what agy-acp reads. Auth needed no owner action - the CLI inherited an existing Google sign-in on first invocation. No `models` array is declared on purpose - the ACP catalog is populated at runtime from `agy models`, and inventing ids here would put a guess where a live catalogue belongs.

watcher.label: Watcher
watcher.description: Read-only Watcher on Gemini, started and fed only by the Supervisor (roles/supervisor.md, Watcher section). Built on the agy-acp ACP bridge like gemini-peer, so roles/*.md cannot be injected by Paseo; instead AGY_EXTRA_ARGS adds @HOME@/.paseo/watcher to every agy run, and agy loads that directory's AGENTS.md (-> roles/watcher.md) as rules and its .agents/hooks.json as a PreToolUse gate (watcher/watcher-gate.sh). The gate, not the prompt, is the boundary: every tool is denied except run_command of paseo ls|logs|inspect, so the seat cannot read or write files, run other commands, or message seats. --dangerously-skip-permissions is required because a hook allow does not grant headless permission; the hook deny still wins (verified 2026-09-30). The directory must stay outside any git repository: agy walks from it to the repo root and would load that repo's AGENTS.md too (verified with the room checkout). No Paseo MCP (supportsMcpServers=false, and watcher is not in injectIntoProviders). Runs on both hosts; on duckling-oci agy is installed as described on gemini-peer.
